newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus falls on Spanish TV talks.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus falls on Spanish TV talks.

text.p: Shares in French pay-TV company Canal Plus were down 1.73 percent at 1,020 francs on volume of 59,752 shares at 1254 GMT, hit by news that its CanalSatellite channel was ready to share rights to screen football matches with Spanish rival Via Digital, market sources said on Tuesday.

CanalSatellite has up to now enjoyed exclusive rights to broadcast first division soccer matches in Spain, but is now ready to negotiate a shared arrangement with Via Digital, Audiovisual Sport said on Monday.
Audiovisual Sport, 40-percent owned by Sogecable, a joint venture between Canal Plus and Spanish publisher Prisa, sold the exclusive rights to CanalSatellite late last year.
Telefonica de Espana is a leading partner in Via Digital.

Market sources also said the Canal Plus stock price was also taking a hit following a ruling against the Paris St Germain football team, in which Canal Plus is a big shareholder, by the UEFA European football authorities.
UEFA has altered PSG's 3-2 defeat in Bucharest last week into a 3-0 loss, after ruling that defender Laurent Fournier was ineligible to play in the match as he had been previously suspended.
French newspapers reported the ruling could cost PSG between 70 and 90 million francs.
